feedback.problem: If the distance between the points $(a+1,a)$ and $(1,-2)$ is minimized, then $a=$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, let's compute the *squared* distance $S(a)$ between the two points. We have

$$
\begin{aligned}S(a) & =(a+1-1)^{2}+(a-(-2))^{2} \\  & =(a)^{2}+(a+2)^{2} \\  & ={a}^{2}+{a}^{2}+4a+4 \\  & =2{a}^{2}+4a+4.\end{aligned}
$$

Since we want to minimize $S,$ we compute the derivative ${S}^{′}(a).$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{S}^{′}(a) & =4a+4.\end{aligned}
$$

The stationary points of $S(a)$ are the points where the derivative ${S}^{′}(a)=0.$ Solving this equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{S}^{′}(a) & =0 \\ 4a+4 & =0 \\ a & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$

We can see that ${S}^{″}(-1)=4>0.$ Therefore, the squared distance (and therefore the actual distance) reaches a minimum when $a=-1.$
